cards.front: What should you know about key principle?
cards.back: Breathing (ventilation) works on the basis of pressure differences . Air always moves from an area of high pressure to an area of low pressure. By changing the volume of the thorax (chest cavity), the body changes the pressure inside the lungs, causing air to move in or out.

cards.front: What should you know about inspiration is an active process?
What should you know about quiet expiration at rest is a passive process?
cards.back: - it does not require muscle contraction. It relies on the elastic recoil of the lungs and the relaxation of the inspiratory muscles.

cards.front: What should you know about forced expiration during exercise is an active process.?
cards.back: The internal intercostal muscles contract to pull the ribs down and in more forcefully. The abdominal muscles also contract, pushing the diaphragm up and compressing the lungs to expel air more quickly.

cards.front: What should you know about during exercise, both the rate and depth of breathing increase?
cards.back: to meet the higher demand for oxygen and to remove more carbon dioxide.
